source.title: Bounding generalization error with input compression: An empirical study with infinite-width networks
source.authors: A. Galloway; A. Golubeva; Mahmoud Salem; M. Nica; Yani Ioannou; Graham W. Taylor

page_placements.theme: Regularization and capacity controls have setting-dependent effects

record.tranche_reason: Applies the training-label randomization test to infinite-width networks, extending the random-label fitting question to this model family.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own random-label training-accuracy results in Table 2 and Figure 4. Other statements about deep networks fitting random labels cite prior work and are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study uses label randomization to evaluate its input compression bound. Its own fitting results concern infinite ensembles of infinite-width NTK networks, equivalent to kernel regression, rather than the standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods named in V1. The authors explicitly caution against extrapolation to finite-width networks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the randomization subsection, but not the paper's overall conclusion. The authors conclude that input compression provides a useful, often non-vacuous generalization bound for infinite-width networks, with limitations in satisfaction rates and error ranking. Label randomization helps diagnose when the bound works; extrapolation to finite-width DNNs remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses two-layer fully-connected infinite-width ReLU NTK networks trained by full-batch gradient descent; compares natural and random labels at matched regularization values. This is not the finite-width standard-network setup of the original studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Random-label fit varies with the diagonal regularization coefficient λ; the paper also reports dataset/task differences in how natural and random training accuracy separate.

fits_no_version.finding: For infinite-width NTK networks on EuroSAT, random-label training accuracy is 71.3%, 89.7%, and 100.0% at λ = 0.1, 0.01, and 0.001; test accuracy is 50.0% in every case. Matched natural-label training accuracies are 97.9%, 99.5%, and 100.0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Infinite-width NTK models can perfectly fit randomized labels at sufficiently low diagonal regularization, while stronger diagonal regularization reduces random-label fitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five datasets, ICB evaluated on natural labels correlates strongly with subsequent random-label training accuracy as λ varies. Natural/random accuracy separation is clearer for MNIST, FashionMNIST, and EuroSAT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input compression measured on natural labels predicts random-label fitting capacity in the tested infinite-width NTK models.

record.problems: The randomization experiment uses a single two-layer fully-connected ReLU network setup and EuroSAT table results; Figure 4 does not provide exact accuracy values in the text. Random-label test error is not reported. Authors caution against extrapolating infinite-width results to finite-width DNNs.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting by standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods; the reported experiments instead use infinite-width NTK ensembles.
Relative training time for true and random labels, and convergence versus corruption fraction.
Training-set fitting with shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Gaussian noise here is a test-time perturbation.
Perfect training fit and test-error degradation across a sweep of label-corruption fractions.

Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting, and true-label generalization after removing them. NTK diagonal regularization does not directly test these interventions.
Temporal ordering of learning shared real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly says random-label test error is unreported: Table 2 reports 50.0% test accuracy for all three randomized-label conditions. States marked cannot_determine reflect the mismatch with the supplied versions, rather than uncertainty about Table 2's numerical results.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test ordinary finite-width deep networks or report test error at chance for random labels.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across corruption fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
No sweep over fractions of corrupted labels or corresponding test-error trend.
Does not test dropout, data augmentation, or whether removing regularization harms true-label generalization.
Does not track whether real-label patterns are learned before random labels.

relation.reason: Applies the randomization test to assess its bound; reports no direct test of a listed claim version in the specified system and training regime.

tranche.reason: Uses label randomization to evaluate an input-compression generalization bound. Its infinite-width kernel models trained by full-batch gradient descent do not test the claim versions about standard deep networks trained with stochastic gradient methods.

source_check.notes: Table 2 supports every reported accuracy, including 50.0% random-label test accuracy at all three regularization values. The authors caution against extrapolating their infinite-width results to finite-width DNNs.
